title: A sharp survival threshold for branching Brownian motion in a self-generated resource environment
summary: We study branching Brownian motion in a resource environment created by the particles themselves. Particles reproduce at rate $β$ times the resource nearby, resource is consumed at rate $c$ times the number of particles nearby, and each death returns resource mass $m$. Let $θ=βm/c$, which represents the number of births supported by resource from one corpse, assuming perfect efficiency. We prove that the population dies out almost surely if $θ\leq1$, even with perfect recycling $\left(θ=1\right)$.
